paper_title: WebGLM Towards An Efficient Web-Enhanced Question Answering System with   Human Preferences
caption: retriever time analysis.

annotations.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the time distribution across different procedures, with a focus on the components labeled as "Search," "Fetch," "Extract," and "Retrieval." The categories are displayed along the horizontal axis, labeled as "Avg.," "50%," "75%," and "90%." The vertical axis represents time, labeled as "sec.," with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 8, with tick marks at intervals of 2 seconds. Each main bar is divided into four stacked segments, representing the different components. The segments for "Search" are dark blue, "Fetch" are medium blue, "Extract" are light blue, and "Retrieval" are lighter blue. The values for these segments vary across the categories. The average ("Avg.") shows "Search" at approximately 2 seconds, "Fetch" at about 2 seconds, "Extract" around less than 0.5 seconds, and "Retrieval" just below 1 second. The "90%" category features the tallest stack, with "Search", "Fetch", and "Retrieval" occupying substantial portions, and a shorter segment for "Extract". The Avg and 75% category cars show a near equal proportion for "Search", "Extract", and "Retrieval" except for "Fetch", with 75% having the largest portion of "Fetch". The bars are not sorted in a particular order beyond the labeled categories, and no specific visual emphasis is applied to any bar. A legend is placed at the top left corner of the plot.
